suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-16 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited cross-national World Mental Health Surveys found agoraphobia commonly co-occurs with depressive and other mental disorders, with coexistence marking more severe presentations. Require independently documented DSM-5 agoraphobia and separately established depressive disorder; under DSM-5 agoraphobia is distinct from panic disorder and must not be inferred from panic attacks or panic disorder alone. The cited cross-national survey reported agoraphobia comorbidity with depressive and other disorders without establishing onset order or direction. Preserve other anxiety disorders, depressive disorders, substance use, medical causes of episodic symptoms, and avoidance attributable to other conditions as competing explanations. Do not present co-occurrence as inevitable progression, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that agoraphobia caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of agoraphobia and depressive-disorder
Chronology compatible with the approved bounded proposition
Assessment of shared risk factors, reverse direction, treatment effects, and other competing causes
